subject: goosebumps on skin
title: Goosebumps Look Useless. Scientists Found Their Hidden Job

scenes.text: Goosebumps look useless on you. They're secretly doing a second job.
Each bump is a tiny muscle pulling one hair upright, a leftover from ancestors with fur.
Fluffed fur traps warm air. On you, there's almost nothing to fluff.
But in 2020, Harvard scientists found the nerve behind that muscle also wires into hair stem cells.
In mice, long cold spells made that nerve wake the stem cells, and new hair started growing.
So the shiver on your arm isn't only about now. It's your body ordering a warmer coat.

description:
Goosebumps are made by tiny arrector pili muscles that raise each hair, a leftover from furry ancestors.
In a 2020 study in Cell, Harvard researchers found the sympathetic nerve that controls this muscle also connects to hair follicle stem cells; in mice, prolonged cold made the nerve activate those stem cells and promote new hair growth.
What gives you goosebumps fastest?
first_comment: Music, cold, or a scary movie: what gives you goosebumps fastest?
